summary: Quarterly commitment checkpoint: Astaglobe wants to finalize capacity uplift pattern (steady + burst), add EU and APAC regions, and align on contract amendment and compliance docs for Private/VPC options. Agreement in principle to pilot Dedicated burst in EU, customer requests SOC2 artifacts and KMS details. Action items assigned for pricing, benchmarks, and documentation.

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Myers: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from Redwood, i can see michael, rita, tomas, elena. does that match?
[00:09] Michael Chen: yep that's us, hey jordan, thanks. we've got about 45 mins, want to make sure we lock down the uplift pattern and the geo timeline.
[00:16] Jordan Myers: perfect, quick agenda: recap current committed capacity, proposed 3x burst for marketing spikes, EU and APAC add, and compliance ask for the private deployment. then action items. sound good?
[00:28] Rita Alvarez: yes and also we need details on network peering and VPC setup — our security team will insist on a prescriptive diagram.
[00:35] Priya Patel: + i'll cover perf and some pre-warm strategies, and what Dedicated looks like under sustained vs burst load.
[00:42] Tomás Nascimento: and i'll flag the compliance side — we need KMS/HSM specs and audit log retention.
[00:48] Jordan Myers: great — quick recap of current: you're on hosted API with a monthly commit of 200k tokens/day, average p95 latency 180ms us-east to eu users at the moment via edge routing, correct?
[01:05] Michael Chen: that's right, but user growth in EMEA means our p95 there is creeping toward 350ms during peaks and that's unacceptable for the chat flow. We want EU region with lower latency and a burst model for campaign days.
[01:18] Priya Patel: got it. for eu activation we recommend a Dedicated pool in eu-west1 with burst reservation that can be pre-warmed. the difference: hosted is more elastic but you see cross-region egress and slightly higher avg latency. Dedicated lets you pin capacity and reduce cold startup by 40-60% in our tests.
[01:35] Rita Alvarez: what's the expected time to provision dedicated capacity in eu? like from purchase to live?
[01:41] Jordan Myers: typically 7-10 business days for reserved capacity after PO clears; for a pilot with limited burst we can do a staged provisioning in 3-5 days if you accept an initial soft-SLA and our ops team handles pre-warm.
[01:55] Michael Chen: and costs — i assume burst is billed differently? we need the delta breakdown per-token, and what gets counted as burst vs steady.
[02:03] Jordan Myers: yes, we'll send a sheet — burst is priced as a premium on top of base reserved unit price; we show both on console and can export per-token. we'll include examples for a 3x burst and hourly granularity so you can model campaigns.
[02:18] Tomás Nascimento: on private options — we're evaluating VPC Private with customer-managed network. can you confirm KMS integration for our keys and whether you support HSM-backed KMS?
[02:29] Priya Patel: we support KMS integrations with common cloud KMS providers and HSM-backed keys via our Private offering. small caveat: some field names in the audit logs are different in the API vs our dashboard, we'll share mapping.
[02:44] Elena Park: is there a way to run a short on-prem or air-gapped pilot? some of our regulatory use cases might require it.
[02:51] Jordan Myers: yes, we have an on-prem package; it's heavier lift but doable. for the initial go-fast we'd recommend Private VPC in your cloud account, then evaluate on-prem for regulated workloads.
[03:05] Michael Chen: timeline question — we want EU live before Jan 15 2026. is that realistic?
[03:11] Priya Patel: yes — assuming approvals this month and the PO in the next two weeks we can hit mid-Jan. the critical path is contract amendment and network setup.
[03:20] Rita Alvarez: network wise we'll need NAT, VPC peering, specific CIDR ranges and a dedicated route table. can you post the exact requirements?
[03:28] Jordan Myers: absolutely — action: i'll send the network diagram and required CIDR list.
[03:32] Speaker 1 (intern): [inaudible]
[03:34] Michael Chen: sorry was that alex? ignore.
[03:36] Jordan Myers: no worries. on performance: priya, can you outline the benchmark plan?
[03:40] Priya Patel: sure. proposed plan: 1) synthetic latency sweep for common seq lengths (64, 128, 512), 2) our KV cache prefix tests to validate cold vs warm starts, 3) throughput run with burst shaping. we'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and token-per-second. goal is to mirror your production prompt distribution.
[04:00] Michael Chen: a note — our prompts are chatty, average 250 tokens per request, short context but frequent system messages. that affects KV and cache behavior.
[04:11] Priya Patel: noted. we'll adapt the harness. also fyi quantization profiles can give you cost savings, but there is a small quality delta. we can recommend profiles per workload.
[04:25] Tomás Nascimento: for compliance, what exact SOC2 artifacts do you provide? we need control narratives and the list of subservice orgs.
[04:34] Jordan Myers: we'll share SOC2 Type II report, controls matrix, and the network diagram. tomas, can you send a short checklist of your required items and I'll deliver what's available?
[04:44] Tomás Nascimento: yes i'll do that — also want to see KMS key rotation cadence and whether logs include plaintext or only pointers.
[04:53] Priya Patel: logs never include plaintext for customer data; we log pointers and metadata, and the audit logs have request ids and token counts.
[05:03] Elena Park: about contract amendment: we're proposing to extend for 12 months with an option to increase reserved capacity in month 3 after pilot. can you support that flexible amendment?
[05:12] Jordan Myers: yes our contracts support mid-term amendments and staged capacity increases; we can draft a rider that outlines the 3-month review and bump options.
[05:21] Michael Chen: also do you have an option for a short-term uplift (like 48-72 hour burst) without permanent commit? marketing runs black-friday style bursts.
[05:30] Jordan Myers: yes we offer transient burst credits; it's priced higher but doesn't force you into long term reserve. we'll include examples in the pricing deck.
[05:39] Rita Alvarez: do we get per-route observability? e.g., to see cost & latency per model and per API key?
[05:45] Priya Patel: yes that's Redwood Console — token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency charts, and trace hooks. we'll attach screenshots.
[05:55] Michael Chen: quick competitor check — MegaCloud AI pitched a blended reserved + spot model that sounded cheaper. what are your differences?
[06:03] Jordan Myers: short answer: we focus on predictable economics + observability; MegaCloud leans on spot instances which can be cheaper but less predictable and sometimes higher cold-starts. InferServe was mentioned as well; they have strong open-source roots but fewer enterprise controls.
[06:18] Priya Patel: from a technical POV, Redwood's serving runtime manages KV caches and continuous batching so you often get better p95s at equivalent cost compared to naive spot approaches.
[06:30] Tomás Nascimento: ok back to timeline — if we get the PO 11/17, when do you need network peering details?
[06:36] Jordan Myers: we'll need the peering CIDRs and SAML metadata by 11/20 to meet mid-Jan activation.
[06:43] Rita Alvarez: noted. we'll prioritize that.
[06:46] Elena Park: one more on billing — can we get monthly billing exported to our billing system?
[06:51] Jordan Myers: yes CSV exports and a billing API are available.
[06:55] Michael Chen: any known gotchas with EU data residency? we've had vendors route logs through us-west and that caused issues.
[07:03] Priya Patel: for Private or Dedicated in EU we keep control plane in region; we will document where logs land and can set retention windows per your policy. we'll include a mapping doc.
[07:14] Jordan Myers: recap — agreed action: Jordan send pricing and network diagram by 11/14; Priya send benchmark plan by 11/18; Tomás send compliance checklist by 11/14. pilot kickoff target 11/19, with EU live mid-Jan pending PO.
[07:29] Michael Chen: that's right, thanks. anything else on questions?
[07:33] Tomás Nascimento: one small ask — encryption in transit details and TLS cert rotation schedule.
[07:38] Priya Patel: we'll include TLS cert rotation cadence and cipher suite details in the security pack.
[07:44] Jordan Myers: perfect. we'll follow up in email with the attachments. thanks everyone.
[07:48] Elena Park: thanks all.
[07:50] [call ends]
